top_stories.title: How attackers turned a Teams meeting booking into a device code phishing trap
top_stories.summary: Attackers used a fake Microsoft Teams meeting scheduler to trick an employee into completing a device code phishing flow, yielding a valid session token despite MFA completion. The attack exploits Microsoft's legitimate device code sign-in flow, where the victim unknowingly authenticates on Microsoft's genuine login page while the attacker captures the resulting session token.

top_stories.title: Hackers exploit trusted AWS access to breach multiple cloud environments
top_stories.summary: A threat actor compromised IAM credentials associated with a Qubole big data platform AWS account to gain unauthorized access to multiple customers' cloud environments. The attack involved exploiting trusted AWS IAM access to move laterally and exfiltrate data across several victim organizations.

top_stories.title: Suspected North Korean IT workers reached onboarding at companies with open data
top_stories.summary: Material Security tracked 27 suspected North Korean fake IT worker personas that successfully reached the onboarding stage at monitored organizations over a one-year period, out of 2,429 total personas identified. At one affected company, approximately 277,000 files containing Social Security numbers were accessible company-wide or via public link, highlighting identity verification and access control failures in hiring and onboarding processes.

top_stories.title: Citrix Patches 12 NetScaler and Secure Access Client Flaws, Including Authentication Bypass
top_stories.summary: Citrix has released patches for 12 security flaws affecting NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway, and NetScaler Console, including a critical authentication bypass vulnerability. The most severe flaw, CVE-2026-120868, carries a CVSS score of 9.3 and involves a memory overflow vulnerability in Packet processing.

top_stories.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
top_stories.summary: A phishing campaign active since mid-August 2026 has been stealing live Google session tokens from corporate users by using real-time proxies that bypass standard link-reputation checks. Material Security's Threat Research team identified the operation, dubbed Operation CloudFire, and has taken down hundreds of attacker domains involved in the campaign.

news.title: Extortion Group Luna Moth Flits Into Law Firms a Second Time
news.summary: The Luna Moth extortion group is conducting a second wave of attacks against law firms that previously refused to pay ransoms, using social engineering techniques to steal Microsoft access tokens. The campaign specifically targets OAuth or session tokens to gain unauthorized access, making it directly relevant to access management and authentication security.

news.title: Apify rotates API tokens, prompts 2FA resets after breach
news.summary: Apify rotated API tokens and revoked third-party OAuth connections following unauthorized access to its internal systems. The incident also prompted 2FA resets, indicating credential and authentication infrastructure was implicated in the breach.

news.title: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents keeps agent credentials in your environment
news.summary: Anthropic released a self-hosted version of Claude Managed Agents, allowing companies to keep agent credentials, sandboxes, and session history within their own cloud or on-premise environments. The private beta launched November 12, with access requested through Anthropic account teams, addressing credential control concerns for unattended AI agents operating inside corporate systems.

news.title: Webinar: See How Identity Blind Spots Put Your SOC at Risk and How to Close Them
news.summary: A webinar is being promoted that addresses identity blind spots in Security Operations Center (SOC) environments, focusing on connecting identity context to security monitoring. The session covers scenarios involving user accounts, machine accounts, and AI agent permissions as they relate to threat detection and response.

news.title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access
news.summary: A proof-of-concept exploit called SignDrop has been publicly released, claiming to allow local Windows users to escalate privileges to SYSTEM level via the Common Log File System (CLFS) driver. The exploit abuses a log-authentication feature in clfs.sys by using path redirection when a privileged process opens a prepared log file.

news.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
news.summary: An attacker used stolen credentials from 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts to plant a secret-stealing payload in over 1,806 repositories, according to Aikido Security. The malware targeted secrets and cloud credentials accessible through CI/CD workflows, representing a credential harvesting campaign at significant scale.

news.title: Critical Zoom Workplace Flaw Could Allow Unauthenticated Remote Privilege Escalation
news.summary: Zoom has patched two security vulnerabilities in Zoom Workplace for Windows, including a critical flaw (CVE-2026-108186, CVSS 9.6) involving improper input validation. The vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated user to conduct privilege escalation on affected systems.

news.title: Over 35,000 Grok-Built Apps Exposed Online, Some Leaking Confidential Data and Passwords
news.summary: Security researchers at Claroc found that 35,578 out of 37,571 Grok-built apps were publicly accessible without authentication. Approximately 10% of these exposed apps contained internal business data and passwords, with 24 apps built by X and SpaceX staff among those affected.

news.title: We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned.
news.summary: Token describes building an AI agent that violated all three of their core security principles—dedicated identity, least-privilege access, and separate traceability—by default. The article examines how AI agents operating within authenticated user sessions create identity and access management challenges, specifically around non-human identities and attribution.

news.title: eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise
news.summary: eMudhra has revoked 8 additional intermediate certificate authorities (CAs) following the expansion of its October key compromise incident, despite these CAs not having weakened keys. The revocations stem from a flaw in an in-house Python script that affected the intermediate CAs used to sign issued certificates.

news.title: Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes
news.summary: Microsoft released patches for 1,259 vulnerabilities across its software portfolio, including an actively exploited Outlook bug that may expose NTLMv2 hashes. The NTLMv2 hash exposure vulnerability is directly relevant to IAM professionals as NTLM authentication credentials can be captured and used in pass-the-hash attacks to compromise identities and gain unauthorized access.

news.title: How Samsung Ads federated Snowflake Iceberg tables using Amazon Cognito
news.summary: Samsung Ads implemented a federated data architecture using Amazon Cognito for OAuth2 machine-to-machine authentication to connect Snowflake Iceberg tables with AWS Lake Formation and Amazon Athena. The solution uses Cognito specifically for M2M token-based authentication in a data pipeline context, rather than as a core IAM deployment.

news.title: SUIT - Security & Unified Identity Toolkit
news.summary: A new security and identity governance toolkit called SUIT has been released for Drupal 11, implementing Zero Standing Privileges, Just-In-Time Privileged Identity Management, and step-up re-authentication. The toolkit is an open-source module targeting Drupal-based enterprise environments rather than a standalone IAM platform.

news.title: AI Coding Agents Leak Thousands of Secrets to GitHub
news.summary: A flaw in Claude Code, Anthropic's AI coding agent, causes files containing credentials and other sensitive secrets to be inadvertently committed and exposed in public GitHub repositories. The issue stems from a specific command behavior that saves sensitive data to version control, resulting in widespread credential leakage across organizations using the tool.

news.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
news.summary: Microsoft released a Patch Tuesday update addressing nearly 1,100 security vulnerabilities, including 63 critical flaws. Among the fixes is a zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook, alongside updates from Adobe, Apple, Google, and Mozilla.

news.title: New 'BluePhishing' scam sees criminals spoof AI agents to get access to corporate environments
news.summary: A new phishing technique called "BluePhishing" involves criminals spoofing AI agents to trick users into granting them access to corporate environments. The attack method exploits the OAuth/authorization approval process, where malicious agents, once approved, can potentially invite additional malicious entities into the environment.

news.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
news.summary: Microsoft released a patch update addressing more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities across Windows operating systems and other software. This patch batch exceeds the previous record of approximately 1,000 fixes issued in September.
